stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown

Use this procedure when handling a puzzle in a Continual-ARC stream.

Preserve each demo as the complete grid as received and compare complete returned grids exactly; do not substitute a sparse reconstruction or hand-derived expected output, since fixture transcription errors can masquerade as rule failures. After each code edit, rerun every pair; an exception or mismatch means the program is not validated, so do not submit yet. Once all pairs match, run it on the test grid and submit only that returned grid. Keep one action JSON object as the last line of every puzzle reply.
4. After a submission verdict, replace the task file with the version that reproduces all available demos, then finish only when the instance is over. Do not claim a task-specific rule is reusable unless it is supported by evidence beyond that instance.

def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    bg = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row).most_common(1)[0][0]
